decision_points.question: what decision rule determines whether the exposure effect counts as statistically supported?
decision_points.why_rival: each defines a different verdict criterion (uncorrected p<0.05, p<0.10, a p+direction+CI rule, a four-tier scheme, or sweeping thresholds); an analyst adopts one rule to declare support

decision_points.question: how is the study's overall conclusion framed?
decision_points.why_rival: both pick the headline narrative — a discordant 'not supported' vs. one centered on cross-league heterogeneity — and the primary write-up leads with one framing

decision_points.question: how is the skin-tone rating variable coded?
decision_points.why_rival: settles which skin-tone coding scheme is used (default vs. the flagged-but-unused alternative)

decision_points.question: where is the continuous skin-tone rating dichotomized?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the cutoff at which the exposure is split, chosen by scanning crude risk-difference shifts

decision_points.question: on what scale is the focal exposure coefficient reported?
decision_points.why_rival: both keep the effect on the raw log-odds/link scale rather than exponentiating to an odds ratio; the effect is reported on one scale

decision_points.question: how is model discrimination / predictive performance assessed?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the validation approach (in-sample AUC without a held-out test set)

decision_points.question: how is the specification-comparison summary populated?
decision_points.why_rival: the panel is either assembled from actual per-spec computed results or filled with hardcoded/fabricated numbers — one source feeds it

decision_points.question: how are the per-league values in the forest plot obtained?
decision_points.why_rival: settles whether forest-plot per-league ORs are manually hardcoded rather than computed

decision_points.question: what outcome model (distribution and link) is used for the primary analysis?
decision_points.why_rival: Poisson-rate, identity-link binomial, probit binomial, logit binomial, and Bayesian DP profile regression are mutually exclusive choices of the primary model form

decision_points.question: what minimum games-together threshold is used to include a dyad?
decision_points.why_rival: one fixes the cutoff at ≥2 games while the other sweeps 2–5; both settle the dyad-inclusion threshold

decision_points.question: how are games-played binned for the descriptive plot?
decision_points.why_rival: both define the game-count binning used in the descriptive plot

decision_points.question: are high-frequency referees excluded from the analysis?
decision_points.why_rival: settles whether referees with >10 games are dropped and the model refit

decision_points.question: is the adjusted analysis stratified by position subgroup, and at what granularity?
decision_points.why_rival: both settle whether/how the adjusted model is split across position subgroups (each position vs. broad groups)

decision_points.question: how is player position operationalized in the model?
decision_points.why_rival: goalkeepers-as-own-category, 3 broad groups, amid/cback dummies, a binary defensive indicator, and the detailed position variable are rival representations of position

decision_points.question: which leagues are included in the league subgroup analysis?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the set of leagues restricted into the subgroup analysis

decision_points.question: what covariates and interactions make up the adjusted design matrix?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the full adjustment set including position, rater interactions, and club

decision_points.question: how is birth year derived from the birthday field?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the parsing method for extracting birth year

decision_points.question: is the exposure effect examined within games-played subgroups?
decision_points.why_rival: settles whether the darkSkin effect is estimated separately within game-count bins

decision_points.question: how are the binomial trial/failure counts defined for the outcome?
decision_points.why_rival: settles how non-red-card 'failures' are constructed from games minus red cards

decision_points.question: how are logically-inconsistent dyad records (cards exceeding games) handled?
decision_points.why_rival: settles disposition of dyads whose total cards exceed games played

decision_points.question: how many positions are shown in the position-breakdown plot?
decision_points.why_rival: top-10 vs top-8 are rival choices of how many positions the breakdown plot displays

decision_points.question: how is the rating distribution compared between red-carded and overall games?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the comparison method (integer-binned chi-square of the rating distribution)

decision_points.question: how are league-specific effect estimates obtained?
decision_points.why_rival: refitting the adjusted model per league, stratifying the crude risk difference by league, or backing out ORs from interaction coefficients are rival ways to produce per-league estimates
